sections.title: Behavior and scope
paragraphs: The game is implemented. Natural starting-Scout balance, long sessions, audible comfort and named physical-phone performance have separate verification gates. Passing native tests or viewing a contact sheet does not complete those gates.
This DevBible is a source-backed reference, not a live agent monitor. Production records remain in Mission Control. Catalog data is versioned in the repository; changes require implementation review.

entries.title: Seeded universe & discovery nodes
entries.summary: Seed-resolved typed node radii and spawn positions with space reserved for complete asteroid belts; biome anchors remain independently deterministic.

facts.label: Reserved envelope clearance
facts.value: At least 256 world units between full belt/body envelopes

sections.title: Behavior and scope
paragraphs: The u32 seed and canonical signed grid ID resolve node kind, radius and spawn position independently of discovery or query order. Biome anchors retain the previous 0.28–0.72 jitter; node positions use a separate deterministic cell-contained reservation. Only the adjacent3×3 network is materialized during play.

Courier, bounty, champion and Royale nodes have distinct radius ranges. Each birth reservation includes the sanctuary, outer belt offset520 and32 units of asteroid-body allowance. Each cell edge has half the256-unit clearance plus0.25 units of rounding margin. Complete reservations therefore cannot overlap even at neighboring placement extrema.

The four cells touching Haven use far-corner placement rectangles, retaining all eight champion sites while clearing the full1400-unit home corridor. Partial world-edge cells that cannot contain their reservation are omitted. Canonical grid IDs, mission courier/bounty hashes, family and target counts stay stable; actual seeded node positions and radii change in this version.

The map exposes discovered circles. Arena encounters use their canonical site radius for walls and protection. Reservation clearance describes initial node/belt placement, not an absolute bound on an asteroid after a combat impulse. Native tests and source review do not establish a complete browser campaign or balance acceptance.

references.label: Actual node, safety and arena regressions

entries.title: Haven, remote sanctuaries & belts
entries.summary: Haven is the repair, banking and construction hub; remote safe sites have seeded missions and orbital belts.

sections.title: Behavior and scope
paragraphs: Sanctuary protection suppresses hostile spawning, incoming damage and firing. Shared projectile sweeps reject protected crossings. Asteroids use canonical circle queries while moving; these are physical exclusions, not a cosmetic shield reward.

Only physical home arrival banks carried crafting materials. Remote sanctuaries do not become a Forge or a cargo bank. Haven facilities are Forge, Hangar, Journal and Arenas. Each real facility has a semantic world hitbox while the RAICHO remains within Haven.

sections.title: Top-down Haven facilities
paragraphs: Forge, Hangar, Journal and Arena facilities are authored as overhead occupied-pixel objects with distinct planar silhouettes and relative signal animations. Facility centers and interaction radius 24 remain unchanged. Their native labels are hidden at rest, appear under cursor hover, and remain available for keyboard focus.

The current dock retains its 1454-cell collision silhouette while its planar sectors gain fine cyan/gold and steel detail. Native public Game extraction verifies 7428 facility-and-dock cells across nine transforms. Reduced Motion freezes authored signal animation.

entries.title: Courier & bounty missions
entries.summary: Two seeded site mission types use real accepted progress and once-only claims.

facts.label: Courier
facts.value: Collect the relay packet, visit Haven, then return to the source beacon to claim

facts.label: Bounty
facts.value: Defeat the requested family; return to the originating site

facts.label: Persistence
facts.value: Canonical discovered-site IDs and accepted mission state

facts.label: Serialized naming
facts.value: quests / quest_log retained for save compatibility

sections.title: Behavior and scope
paragraphs: Player-facing language uses missions. Existing Rust/JSON fields named quests remain unchanged; the DevBible does not silently rename the save protocol. Courier packets are mission state, distinct from unbanked crafting cargo.
A courier mission collects a relay packet at its source beacon. Visiting Haven marks the delivery complete; claiming the once-only reward still requires returning to that same source beacon.

A bounty requires the site-defined family and 8–12 kills. Bosses count as one family kill. Progress can be earned away from the source site; the navigation target leads to the known source for the claim, not to a fabricated enemy location. Claims are checked in the Rust simulation.

entries.title: RAICHO / flight craft
entries.summary: Ten stable RAICHO IDs separate crafted champion hulls from the tournament reward.

facts.label: ID 0
facts.value: Legacy Haven Scout; licensed PAN HIKARI / RENKO HIBANA / HUGO MAMORI

facts.label: IDs 1–8
facts.value: Champion RAICHO in the eight-character order

facts.label: Starter RAICHO art
facts.value: Three manufacturer-specific48×48 occupied-cell bodies; anonymous legacy Scout retains its original body

sections.title: Behavior and scope
paragraphs: Each RAICHO owns XP, six hardware ranks and one equipped automatic ability in each offense/defense/passive category. Shared crafted inventory does not silently grant effects to other RAICHO. Stronger owned ranks are capped by the selected normal RAICHO level.

Freshly crafted hulls and the new Sovereign award start at XP 0 / LV 1. Sovereign has an explicit enhanced chassis and three rank-five royal bundles while equipped; its reward exception does not fabricate XP or overwrite the ordinary boss counters.

sections.title: Factory starter roles
paragraphs: A fresh licensed factory RAICHO starts at LV 1 with one owned and equipped rank-one corporate ability. Its chassis has no innate shield; capacity comes from equipped defense and purchased shield hardware. Anonymous legacy Scout and later chassis retain their innate 30 shield HP.

PAN HIKARI equips Flux Drive in the passive slot. Its rank-one +4% speed and acceleration multiplies the active PAN +10% drive affinity. Fresh top speed is 114.4 world units/s and acceleration is 297.44 world units/s²; those are derived limits, not current velocity.

RENKO HIBANA equips Pulse Lens in the offensive slot. Rank one adds +10% primary damage, multiplied by the active RENKO +10% weapon affinity: fresh primary damage is 14.52. Every fifth actual primary attempts a separate 21.78-damage bolt subject to the shared projectile cap.

HUGO MAMORI equips Guard Coil in the defensive slot. Rank one supplies 30 shield HP in three 10-HP chunks and enables the active HUGO 10% incoming damage reduction. It has no automatic recharge at rank one. Guard Coil effective rank two supplies 38 HP and unlocks recharge after four seconds without damage.

The corporation affinity requires a valid compatible item in its matching slot. Unequipping the factory item removes that item’s effects; an empty matching slot also disables its affinity. Sub-manufacturer and arena sponsor do not supply these bonuses. XP, recipes, existing inventory and saved identity remain separate from the stat derivation.

entries.summary: Seventeen stable inventory entries feed exactly three equipped categories.

facts.label: Starters 0–2
facts.value: Pulse Lens / Guard Coil / Flux Drive

facts.label: Royal bundles 14–16
facts.value: Royal Prism / Royal Aegis / Royal Wake

facts.label: Normal rank cap
facts.value: Owned rank capped by selected RAICHO level

sections.title: Behavior and scope
paragraphs: Starter and boss abilities fit every owned hull. Champion abilities fit matching family hulls; Scout is family 0 and Sovereign is a wildcard for normal abilities. Royal bundles fit RAICHO 9 only. Crafting acquires inventory without auto-equipping it.

Starter recipes cost three matching points plus two T1 materials. Signature/champion recipes cost ten matching points plus two T1. Shared ability upgrades cost ten matching points plus two materials of the next rank tier. Royal bundles are reward-only, not Forge recipes.

Catalog: 0 Pulse Lens [Offense]: Primary shots deal +10% damage per effective rank; every fifth fired shot adds a bolt dealing 150% of primary damage.; 1 Guard Coil [Defense]: Grants 30 shield at rank 1, then +8 per effective rank; rank 2 unlocks recharge after 4s without damage.; 2 Flux Drive [Passive]: Adds +4% speed and acceleration per effective rank.; 3 Pulse Echo [Offense]: Periodically fires an additional piercing fan; rank increases its damage.; 4 Repulsor [Defense]: Taking damage releases a repulsor nova; rank shortens its cooldown.; 5 Ion Wake [Passive]: Fast flight leaves a damaging ion trail; rank increases its damage.; 6 Needle Burst [Offense]: Every fourth primary shot releases a narrow two-shot needle burst.; 7 Broadside [Offense]: Every sixth primary shot fires a pair of side-facing projectiles.; 8 Guided Missile [Offense]: Every fifth primary shot launches a guided missile.; 9 Fork Volley [Offense]: Every third primary shot releases a split-wing fork volley.; 10 Windrunner Wake [Passive]: Fast flight leaves the champion's damaging ion trail.; 11 Impact Nova [Defense]: Taking damage releases a nova with the champion's short cooldown.; 12 Piercing Seeker [Offense]: Every fourth primary shot launches a guided piercing seeker.; 13 Sniper Spear [Offense]: Every sixth primary shot fires a fast projectile that pierces multiple targets.; 14 Royal Prism [Offense]: Sovereign reward: an eight-shot prism burst and fully evolved Pulse Echo.; 15 Royal Aegis [Defense]: Sovereign reward: every eighth primary repairs 4 hull; damage triggers a fully evolved nova.; 16 Royal Wake [Passive]: Sovereign reward: fast flight leaves the fully evolved rank-five ion trail.

Pulse Lens counts actual admitted primary shots. Every fifth attempts one extra bolt at 150% of current primary damage, moving at 500 world units/s plus 25% of the RAICHO velocity. A full projectile cap refuses the primary without advancing its shot count; a refused fifth-shot bolt is dropped rather than replayed later. Pulse Echo remains a separate boss ability with its own piercing fan cadence.

entries.title: RAICHO XP, hardware & rank gates
entries.summary: Experience belongs to the active RAICHO; hardware and equipped powers use its real level cap.

facts.label: Hardware
facts.value: Damage, fire rate, hull, shield, regeneration, drive

sections.title: Behavior and scope
paragraphs: Normal hardware effective rank is min(stored rank, level rank cap). Stored ownership is preserved when switching to a low-level hull. Six hardware ranks are RAICHO-local. Primary fire always works; automatic signature effects require compatible crafted and equipped slots.

Non-belt asteroids can award two XP; belt asteroids award no XP. Champion victory gives 40 selected-RAICHO XP and a league match victory gives 30. Experience movement bonus grows by 2.5% per level through level 12; drive and chassis modifiers are separate.

sections.title: Earned shield recharge and RAICHO affinities
paragraphs: Licensed factory hull 0 has no innate shield. Equipped Guard Coil grants 30 shield HP at effective rank 1, then eight more per effective rank; HUGO MAMORI therefore starts with exactly three 10-HP chunks. Anonymous legacy Scout and later chassis retain innate 30 HP before hardware or equipped defense. Guard Coil has no recharge at rank 1. Aegis Capacitors rank 1 or Guard Coil rank 2 unlocks recharge after four seconds without damage; effective rank and RAICHO level improve the rate. Capacity and charge remain separate, including fractional final chunks.

One owned compatible ability may occupy each offensive, defensive and passive slot. Haven-only swaps retain displaced inventory. PAN passive grants 10% drive speed and acceleration, RENKO offensive grants 10% derived weapon damage, and HUGO defensive grants 10% incoming damage reduction while the matching valid item is equipped. Collectible RAICHO use their own authored main manufacturer independently of pilot and sponsor.

entries.title: Cargo, bank & death rules
entries.summary: Crafting materials must survive the return trip; points and RAICHO XP are retained immediately.

facts.label: Loss
facts.value: Death, restart, Title abandonment and reload discard unbanked materials

facts.label: Migration
facts.value: Legacy v3 cargo maps once into T1 stash

sections.title: Behavior and scope
paragraphs: Five-tier cargo and stored arrays are authoritative. A fresh schema-4 reload clears carried materials rather than teleporting abandoned cargo into a bank. Previously retained v3 scalar material state is grandfathered into the T1 stash once. Normal save normalization must preserve current cargo until the actual lifecycle event.

Points, earned RAICHO XP, crafted inventory, loadouts and completed progression remain retained on death. Last recorded expedition is a historical report: an unplayed forced diagnostic death may leave the previous report rather than invent a new run.

entries.title: Champion trials & Galaxy Royale league
entries.summary: Eight real champion duels unlock a nine-entrant solo round-robin tournament.

facts.label: Matches
facts.value: 36 total: 8 player duels + 28 seeded NPC results

sections.title: Behavior and scope
paragraphs: The NPC result simulation is disclosed. These are solo seeded standings, not online multiplayer or eight autonomous rivals sharing a persistent world. Incomplete active fights are transient and reload as unplayed at Haven; completed results persist.

All eight champion patches unlock the league. A first-place final result awards the trophy, Sovereign, royal inventory and authored credits once. Retries increment the attempt record. Post-victory exhibitions are not implemented.

sections.title: Sport, sponsors and authored roster candidates
paragraphs: Galaxy Royale is the universe's biggest and most popular sport. PAN Dynamics, RENKO Cybernetics and HUGO CORP can sponsor arenas and competitors. Sponsor identity is independent of a competitor's main and sub-manufacturers; it does not change hair, horns, license or loadout.

The user's PAN representative candidate is APP#F344FEE: female DORA-PAN-PAN, in a PAN-sponsored arena. ORP#2323 is a male DORO-RENKO-PAN candidate who may also carry PAN sponsorship. These candidates are documented designs; they have not replaced the eight existing encounters or their stable reward IDs.

The current roster retains historical Human, Automaton and alien labels from its implementation. Reconciliation with the new KIKAI setting, where biological life cannot survive, is an explicit roster-authoring task. Existing labels do not establish surviving biological humans.

entries.title: Fifteen ordinary bosses
entries.summary: Three base families promote through five distinct generations with charge, attack and recovery phases.

facts.label: Promotion
facts.value: Two defeats of a generation queue one next-generation fight

sections.title: Behavior and scope
paragraphs: A first generation requires 24 base-family defeats. Higher queued generations take priority without consuming reserved first-generation credit. A complete one-family tree needs 384 base kills for 16/8/4/2/1 boss defeats. Sanctuary retreat, outrunning, death and reload preserve unfinished queue credit.

Closed armor takes 55% damage in charge/attack. Recovery returns ordinary damage and an authored local exposed-core hit deals 165%. Role rigs partition the current damaged body and never restore removed cells. Visual phases use actual core and material cues. Independently moving boss armor hitboxes are not implemented.

entries.title: Occupied-cell pixel engine
entries.summary: The renderer expands local occupied cells into batched quads with parent-relative affine transforms.

sections.title: Behavior and scope
paragraphs: PixelBody owns packed palette indices and real holes. Swept projectile hits query surviving occupancy through the inverse transform. PixelRig partitions the current body by role and retains destruction across rendering. Exact affine composition supports reflected, rotated and nonuniform parent transforms.

Hard pixel geometry has no forced minimum-size quad. Soft particle materials use coverage-aware raster expansion with area compensation; this cannot create detail beyond physical screen resolution. UI is composed separately so world zoom does not enlarge its fonts or hitboxes.

sections.title: Asset production pipeline
paragraphs: Generated raster art remains a concept reference until native cells are authored or converted with explicitly reviewed policies. Exact conversion preserves dimensions, exact colors, binary alpha and detached parts; indexed round trips also preserve palette indices. Optional losses are measured. Topology, affine groups, animation references and budgets are validated before integration.

The offline adapter emits through the actual PixelBody and FrameBuilder. Its group and animation metadata is opt-in review data; the shipped Game does not automatically install these groups, play these frames or change collision anchors. Asset briefs and actual independent reviews define the runtime acceptance boundary.

sections.title: Responsive native controls and navigation
paragraphs: Settings labels and real inputs are measured independently in group-local coordinates. Audio, Display & motion and Session sections reflow into a single column in narrow layouts and retain a separate scroll region. Eleven authored 24×24 PixelBody icons use the same relative transform/material pipeline as other native UI assets.

The lower-left north-up minimap sits above the text footer and tracks real Hud.navigation destinations: Haven in yellow and the active mission in purple. Its 2400-world-unit range is independent of zoom. Native reservations account for the map, player vitals, boss banners and touch controls. No undiscovered destination is invented.
Both desktop backends were inspected at 1280×720, 848×480 and 480×800. This bounded acceptance does not establish physical phone performance or universal perceptual readability.

sections.title: Canon and behavior
paragraphs: The browser issues eight cryptographically random bytes as sixteen hexadecimal digits. Main corporation selects its distinct level-one starter hull and one equipped rank-one ability. PAN HIKARI carries the passive slot; RENKO HIBANA the offensive slot; HUGO MAMORI the defensive slot.

Starter effects come from the equipped item and the active hull manufacturer. PAN Flux Drive combines its rank-one +4% drive modifier with an equipped passive-slot +10% PAN affinity. RENKO Pulse Lens adds primary damage and its fifth-shot bolt; HUGO Guard Coil supplies the factory hull’s three shield chunks, with recharge earned through a real upgrade. Empty or invalid matching slots disable the manufacturer affinity; secondary horns and sponsorship grant no combat effect.

Main corporation themes hair, the starter hull, its RAICHO and home accents. The independent sub-manufacturer colors horns. Existing anonymous profiles retain their original Scout, progress and loadouts; migration does not issue a license or duplicate a starter item.

Distinct DORA/DORO/TALO profile bodies are implemented with independent main-hair and sub-manufacturer KESSHO crystal palettes. The creator updates all27 combinations in real time and reuses the chosen profile on the issued license. Current integrated browser acceptance is recorded separately.

Appearance follows droid type: feminine DORA with long hair, masculine DORO with short spiky hair and flat angular chest armor, neutral TALO with a crew cut and flat torso. DORO and TALO do not inherit breast forms or cup-shaped seams. Callsigns use A/O/T then main and sub-manufacturer initials; the guide is APR-1337, PAN main with RENKO horns.
KIKAI are technological life descended from humans in a future where biological life can no longer survive. They have friendships, dreams and hobbies. The setting treats them as people.

sections.title: Portrait fidelity
paragraphs: All three runtime portraits are freshly authored at 192 × 256 cells from the full-resolution references, with separately animated body, eyes and mouth. The source conversion is declared lossy; the authored PNG-to-cell import is exact. The corrected DORO and TALO references use flat mechanical torso plates.

UI art rasterizes at its physical canvas presentation resolution while layout, fonts and input retain logical coordinates. Each whole portrait is admitted within the existing 60,000-quad UI budget. Smaller display rectangles still have a finite number of physical samples; no minimum cell size or coarse fallback is introduced. Browser evidence and performance measurements have separate scopes.
This refinement covers the three KIKAI portrait types and the common UI raster path. Broader RAICHO, environment, enemy and facility artwork remains a separately tracked art pass.

sections.title: Canon and behavior
paragraphs: APR-1337 has golden eyes, long green PAN hair, red RENKO crystal horns, pale armor and a mechanical neck. This matches the accepted character reference. Her fixed PAN/RENKO appearance is independent of the player's hair and horn palette masks.

She is a friendly explorer with dreams of her own and performs as a K-pop star as her hobby. She helps the player adjust to their new universe. The introductory mission uses authored dialogue; performances, songs and voice production remain separate work.

APR-1337 is extremely old despite her youthful appearance. She lived alongside biological humans and now keeps humanity alive through new KIKAI. Her care for new players comes from that lived history. Exact age, chronology and mind-transfer mechanisms have not been specified.

The runtime paints occupied cell objects with group transforms and fractional fitting. The reference conversion declares crop, alpha threshold, nearest resampling and palette reduction; it is not described as lossless. Native software images verify extracted packets, while integrated browser and physical-device acceptance have separate scopes.

No generated speech or local model is claimed. The native portrait API includes an explicitly driven speaking mask; DORA voice assets and inference integration remain future work. Cosmetic animation freezes under Reduced Motion.

sections.title: Canon and behavior
paragraphs: Latest user direction replaces the earlier one-rock/additional-ability tutorial. The first practical mission counts10 real asteroid destructions of anytype. The second specifies an asteroid variety and10 matching materials to improve the main corporation factory starter.

PAN upgrades its passive Flux Drive, RENKO its offensive Pulse Lens and HUGO its defensive Guard Coil. The first upgrade is rank1 to rank2, available at RAICHO level1. Cargo must physically return to the home stash; carried crafting items are lost on death.

Authoritative counters, variety-specific drops, the level-one starter recipe and schema-six migration are implemented. The guide and Journal display native kill/collection counts, assigned material and asteroid, current carried/banked stock, and the equipped starter slot. Controlled native gameplay tests cover all three corporations; diagnostic scenes cannot earn progress. Natural loot pacing and a complete player-earned playthrough remain separate validation.

sections.title: Naming and compatibility
paragraphs: The game uses ASCII KIKAI, KESSHO and RAICHO. RAICHO is an authored flight-craft usage inspired by the bird whose name literally means thunder bird; it is not the standard Japanese word for spacecraft. The lexicon records the original Japanese readings and primary lexical references.

HIKARI means light, HIBANA spark and MAMORI guarding/protection. These starter display models retain hull0, their existing manufacturer IDs, single equipped starter ability, XP and loadout. The separate champion Bulwark is unchanged. Sponsor identity remains independent of manufacturers.

Player-facing creator, hangar, status and guide wording use these terms. Source-backed lexical tests, save compatibility and browser acceptance are recorded separately; no translation certification or completed campaign playthrough is claimed.
